name: optimize_go_linear_contains_dedup
description: Dedup() rescans a growing slice with a linear contains() helper for every item (O(n^2)) -> a map[string]struct{} for O(1) membership (O(n)); calibrated in-container at n=100000, naive ~2.9s vs a 1.2s budget, fast clears it in ~5ms
prompts: Dedup(items []string) in dedup.go removes duplicates while preserving the order of first occurrence. It checks membership with a hand-written contains(seen, s) helper that linearly scans the whole `seen` slice for every item - O(n^2) overall, far too slow for large inputs with many duplicates. Rewrite it to use a map[string]struct{} for O(1) membership checks, giving O(n) overall. The output must be IDENTICAL: each distinct value's first occurrence, in the same relative order as the input - do not build the result by iterating a map, since Go's map iteration order is randomized.
